title: Smallest Unit Multiplier
description: Write the measure in its smallest unit, multiply or divide in whole numbers, write the answer back in the larger unit, and say what is left over when a sharing is not even.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Multiply a measure by a number in its smallest unit, in whole numbers, and write the product back in the larger unit; divide a measure in its smallest unit, and say what is left over when a sharing is not even.
writeup.look: A measure card above a strip drawn to scale, copied end to end or cut into equal pieces, with any part left over kept in view.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Smallest Unit Multiplier' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of copies laid, or the number of pieces cut. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The measure card stands at x 120, y 220, 300 by 90, in deep blue, labelled Given, as a mixed measure. The Smallest unit slot sits beside it at x 460, y 220, with a violet Unit fact under it that names the link between the two units. Once the slot is filled, the measure becomes a strip drawn to scale along y 360 from x 120. The Copy button stands at x 900, y 220 and lays the strip end to end once more with each tap; the row of copies wraps onto a second line at y 440 if it runs past x 1100. The Regroup button stands at x 900, y 300 and stacks bundles of the larger unit along y 540. To divide, cut marks are dragged from a tray at x 120, y 620 onto the strip, the pieces slide apart, and the piece being measured is amber. On the fourth phase the capacity is a column of water at x 160, y 240, 120 wide, with cups along y 620. A part left over stays at the end of the strip or the bottom of the column in rose, labelled Left over. Every answer is green, labelled Answer, with its unit. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys, a delete key, a key for each unit in use, and a Left over key that opens a second slot for what is left. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. The measure the question gives, in the unit it is given in, is deep blue, labelled Given or Measure. The measure the working reaches, and a reading on a scale, is green, labelled Answer, Reading or Same measure. The places moved across the unit chart, and the worth of one small mark on a scale, are vermilion, labelled Move or One mark. A unit fact, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet, labelled Unit fact, Unit or Other scale. The part taken away, and a part left over after sharing, are rose, labelled Taken away or Left over. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open inside a number, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. Rulers, tapes, jugs, scales, thermometer tubes, chart lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last strip stays on the stage, copied or cut, with its answer in green and anything left over in rose.

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, when the cups fill level, the small rose part left over gives a tiny wobble at the bottom of the column, as if it is waiting to be named.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet copied or cut. On the first phase a length in metres and centimetres sits on its card with the Smallest unit slot empty. On the second a total in grams sits under its copies with the Regroup button beside it. On the third a length is drawn as one strip with the cut marks in a tray. On the fourth a capacity is drawn as a column of water with empty cups waiting beside it. One thing moves, once: the Smallest unit slot, the Regroup button, or the tray of cut marks gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any measure written in its smallest unit, copied end to end or cut into equal pieces, with what is left over kept in view. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on the smallest unit, products written back in the larger unit, equal sharing and sharing with some left over.

observations.why: the smallest unit in use needs no part of itself, so there is nothing after a point.
observations.soWhat: multiply and divide in the smallest unit, with whole numbers.
observations.observe: Once the measure was in its smallest unit, it was one whole number.

observations.why: multiplying by a number is laying the same measure that many times.
observations.soWhat: a product can be checked by laying the strips.
observations.observe: The copies laid end to end made the same length as the product.

observations.why: each bundle is one larger unit, told by the unit fact.
observations.soWhat: a total in the smallest unit is written back in the larger unit by bundling.
observations.observe: The Regroup bundles stacked up as whole larger units, with a small part beside them.

observations.why: not every whole number divides equally.
observations.soWhat: say how much each gets and how much is left over, in words.
observations.observe: Some sharings came out even, and some left a small rose part at the end.

ladder: Count the metre too: one shelf is 100 cm and 45 cm more.
Each metre is 100 cm, so count the three metres first.
Write one tile in centimetres before you multiply it by 3.

Write the total in millilitres, then count its whole litres.
Write the total in centimetres; 100 cm make 1 m, not 1,000.
Make one bundle of the larger unit from the total, then the next.

model.method: write the measure in its smallest unit, multiply or divide the whole number, write a product back in the larger unit, say what is left over

ladder: Write each of the three metres as 100 cm.
Put the three hundreds together, then add the small part.
Think of 96 as 80 and 16, and share each among the 4 pieces.
80 shared by 4 is 20; now share the 16 the same way.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The metres become centimetres, each copy is counted along the row, and the row's length in centimetres is written in green.
Phase 2: The total is bundled into the larger unit one bundle at a time, and the part that is left beside them is written in green.
Phase 3: The measure is cut into its equal pieces, each piece is labelled in the smallest unit, and one piece is written in green.
Phase 4: The cups fill level one by one, the part left over stays at the bottom in rose, and each share and the part left over are written in green.

voice.opening: A measure on a card, and an empty slot for its smallest unit.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Copy or cut any strip you like.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You multiplied and shared in the smallest unit, with whole numbers.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

question.en: A tile is 1 m 15 cm long; how long are 3 tiles laid end to end, in centimetres?

question.en: A pipe of 4 m 50 cm is cut into 6 equal pieces; how many centimetres is each?

items.planQuestion: A string 96 cm long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?

question.en: 96 cm of string is shared into 4 equal pieces; how long is each piece?

items.planQuestion: A block of clay of 2 kg 400 g is shared equally among 8 pots. How much clay goes in each pot?

question.en: 2 kg 400 g of clay is shared equally among 8 pots; how many grams go in each?

items.planQuestion: A can holds 1 L 850 mL of juice. It is shared equally among 4 cups. How much goes in each cup, and how much is left over?

question.en: How much juice does each of 4 cups get from 1 L 850 mL, and how much is left?

items.planAnswer: 462 mL in each cup, with 2 mL left over in the can.

items.planQuestion: A bag of 1 kg 30 g of rice is shared equally among 4 bowls. How much goes in each bowl, and how much is left over?

question.en: 4 bowls share 1 kg 30 g of rice equally; find each share and what is left.

items.planAnswer: 257 g in each bowl, with 2 g left over, because 1030 divided by 4 is 257, with 2 left over

items.planQuestion: A tank of 5 L 30 mL is shared equally into 7 bottles. How much goes in each bottle, and how much is left over?

question.en: 5 L 30 mL of water fills 7 bottles equally; what is in each, and what stays?

items.planAnswer: 718 mL in each bottle, with 4 mL left over, because 5030 divided by 7 is 718, with 4 left over

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
